title.title: Checkerboard embeddings of \(\ast\)-graphs into nonorientable surfaces

editorial_contributions.text: In this paper, the authors construct additional gradings on two generalizations of Khovanov homology. Using the cohomology of surfaces, they construct an additional grading on the virtual and doubled Khovanov homology of a link in a thickened surface. Using homotopy classes of curves on surfaces, they construct another grading on the virtual Khovanov homology; these homotopy classes are represented by diagrams, so the resulting grading is called a picture-valued grading. They associate maps between the homology groups to cobordisms between links, and they produce picture-valued invariants of links in thickened surfaces, and picture-valued invariants of surfaces embedded in thickened 3-manifolds. The paper is closed with a list of directions for future work.

title.title: Additional gradings on generalizations of Khovanov homology and invariants of embedded surfaces

editorial_contributions.text:
The groups \(G_n^k\) depending on the two parameters \(k,n\in \mathbb N\), \(n>k\), were defined by V. O. Manturov and they have the following presentation:

A set of generators given by \(\{a_m \mid m\subset\{1,\dots,n\}, \;|m|=k\}\) subject to the relations:

(1) \((a_m)^2=1\) for \(m\subset \{1,\dots,n\}, |m|=k\),

(2) \(a_ma_{m'}=a_{m'}a_m\) for \(m, m'\subset \{1,...,n\}\), \(|m\cap m'|<k-1\),

(3) \(a_{m^1}\dots a_{m^{k+1}}=a_{m^{k+1}}\dots a_{m^1}\) for \(U=\{\iota_1,\dots,\iota_{k+1}\}\subset \{1,\dots,n\}\) and \(m^{\ell}=U\backslash\{\iota_{\ell}\}\).

Invariants of the elements of these groups and homomorphisms from the pure Artin braid groups into \(G_n^k\) have been studied and the results can be used to obtain certain properties of the Artin pure braid groups as well as of knots. These invariants are called \(MN\)-invariants in the paper under review; they will not detect non-trivial Brunnian braids. This is Lemma 4.5, in words, the \(MN\)-invariant of the image of a Brunnian braid in \(G_n^3\) is trivial. 

The main goal of the paper is to introduce a new invariant which is stronger in the sense that it detects Brunnian braids. A new group denoted by \(G_{n,p}^3\) is defined, which has an additional structure called parity, as well as a homomorphism from \(G_{n+1}^3\) to \(G_{n,p}^3\). The new invariant is defined for the elements of \(G_{n,p}^3\) which together with the homomorphisms distinguish the non-triviality of the Brunnian braids. The details are too technical to be written here. The examples 4.11, 4.12, 4.13 illustrate the use of this new invariant.

title.title: On groups \(G_n^k\), braids and Brunnian braids

editorial_contributions.text:
In 2000, Khovanov discovered a homology invariant for links whose Euler characteristic is the Jones polynomial. It is known as Khovanov homology. There are many analogies and extensions of Khovanov homology. In the paper under review, the authors define an extension of Khovanov homology for a link in a thickened closed surface. In particular, they introduce a new grading called the \textit{homotopical grading}.

Let \(S\) be a closed surface. Let \(\mathfrak{L}=[S^{1}, S]\) be the set of all the homotopy classes of free oriented loops in \(S\). Then, define \(\mathfrak{H}\) to be the quotient group of the free abelian group with generator set \(\mathfrak{L}\) modulo the relations: any contractible loop is zero, and a loop and its reverse are equal. Let \(D\) be a diagram in \(S\). As Khovanov homology, for each \(s\in\{0, 1\}^{\chi (D)}\), we obtain the circles \(C_1, C_2, \dots, C_{\gamma(s)}\) of the resolution of \(D\) associated with \(s\), where \(\chi (D)\) is the set of the crossings of \(D\). Then for each element \(x=x_1\otimes x_2 \otimes \dots \otimes x_{\gamma(s)}\in \{v_{\pm }\}^{\gamma(s)}\subset V^{\otimes \gamma(s)}\), we define the \textit{homotopical grading} \(h(x)\) by \(\sum_{i=1}^{\gamma(s)}\text{deg}(x_i)[C_i]\in \mathfrak{H}\), where \(V\) is the Frobenius algebra used in Khovanov homology, and \(\text{deg}(v_{\pm })=\pm 1\).

The authors review a Khovanov homology with coefficients \(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\) for links in a thickened closed surface, and prove that the homotopical gradings are well-defined in the homology (Theorem 2.6). The authors call this homology the \textit{homotopical Khovanov homology}. Moreover, the authors separate crossings of a diagram by using a \textit{parity} of crossings, and define the \textit{homotopical Khovanov homology with respect to the parity} (Theorem 3.6).

Note that there are many differences between the published version and the arXiv version [\url{arXiv:1501.04805v1}].

title.title: Graph-links

editorial_contributions.text:
A classical knot is a smoothly embedded \(S^1\) in \(S^3\). It is well known that a given knot diagram corresponds to a chord diagram, where each chord is assigned with an orientation and a sign. Conversely, this chord diagram also can be used to reconstruct the original knot diagram. By forgetting the orientations and signs of the chords in a chord diagram, one obtains a chord diagram corresponding to a free knot. In other words, a free knot is an equivalence class of chord diagrams (without arrows and signs) under Reidemeister moves.

In the paper under review, the authors study when an odd free knot is slice. Here we say that a free knot is odd if each chord meets an odd number of chords in the chord diagram. In order to state the main result, one needs a pairing which associates each chord with another chord, or itself. If two distinct chords are pairing, one can obtain a new chord diagram by reconnecting the four endpoints of these two chords. The main result of this paper is that an odd free knot is slice if and only if there exists a pairing such that the new chord diagram obtained has no intersections. The proof involves the study of the resolution operation on free 2-knots.

editorial_contributions.text:
The purpose of the paper is to give a categorification for an extension of the Kauffman bracket polynomial called the arrow polynomial, see for example the article by two of the authors [\textit{H. A. Dye} and \textit{L. H. Kauffman}, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 18, No. 10, 1335--1357 (2009; Zbl 1195.57028)]. The arrow polynomial is a polynomial in the infinite set of commuting variables \(A\), \(A^{-1}\) and \(K_n\) (for all positive integers \(n\)), but for any given virtual link the set of variables appearing in the polynomial is finite. The variables \(K_n\) correspond to an integer arrow number calculated from each loop on an oriented state summation for the bracket. The categorifications are based on a new gradings associated with these arrow numbers, and give homology theories associated with oriented virtual knots and links via extra structure on the Khovanov chain complex. As an application the paper concludes with some estimates on the virtual crossing number and the surface genus of virtual knots and links.

For the entire collection see [Zbl 1205.57002].

title.title: On two categorifications of the arrow polynomial for virtual knots

editorial_contributions.text: The paper under review is a continuation of the joint work by the first author and \textit{I. M. Nikonov} [J. Knot Theory Ramifications 24, No. 13, Article ID 1541009, 16 p. (2015; Zbl 1339.20033)]. In [loc. cit.], the authors constructed a homomorphism from the free braid group to free groups. In this paper, the authors extend this construction from free braids to free \(n\)-\(n\) tangles, which include free links. In other words, they define invariants of free \(n\)-\(n\) tangles valued in free groups. The key point of the construction is, if two free \(n\)-\(n\) tangles with no pure crossings (i.e. no strand has a crossing with itself) are equivalent then it is proved that they can be related by a sequence of moves such that all intermediate diagrams have no pure crossings.

editorial_contributions.text:
A virtual diagram is a 4-valent graph in \(\mathbb{R}^2\) with two types of vertices, one of which are classical crossings with a choice for underpass and overpass specified, and the other are virtual crossings marked by small circles. A virtual link is an equivalence class of virtual diagrams modulo generalized Reidemeister moves. Virtual knot theory was introduced by \textit{L. H. Kauffman} [Eur. J. Comb. 20, No.~7, 663--690 (1999; Zbl 0938.57006)]. In the paper under review, an estimate for the number of virtual crossings of virtual links are obtained. 

For a virtual diagram \(D\), let \(\zeta(D)\) be an unnormalized version of the \(\xi\)-polynomial of virtual links introduced independently by several authors, for example, \textit{L. H. Kauffman} and \textit{D. Radford} [in: D. E. Radford (ed.) et al., AMS special session on diagrammatic morphisms in algebra, category theory, and topology, San Francisco, CA, USA, October 21-22, 2000. Providence, RI: American Mathematical Society (AMS). Contemp. Math. 318, 113--140 (2003; Zbl 1031.57009)], \textit{V. O. Manturov} [Russ. Math. Surv. 57, No.~5, 997-998 (2002); translation from Usp. Mat. Nauk 57, No.~5, 141--142 (2002; Zbl 1044.57003)], \textit{J. Sawollek} [J. Knot Theory Ramifications 12, No.~6, 767--779 (2003; Zbl 1051.57013)] and \textit{D. Silver} and \textit{S. Williams} [J. Knot Theory Ramifications 10, No.~1, 151--160 (2001; Zbl 0997.57019)]. 

Then \(\zeta (D)\) is a Laurent polynomial with two variables \(s\) and \(t\). We denote by \(\text{deg}\zeta (D)\) and \(\text{mdeg}\zeta (D)\) the leading (lowest) degree of \(\zeta (D)\) with respect to the variable \(s\). In [\textit{V. O. Manturov}, loc. cit.], the second author of this paper showed that if \(D\) and \(D'\) are equivalent virtual diagrams then \(\zeta (D) = t^l \zeta(D')\) for some integer \(l\). Therefore, \(\text{deg}\zeta (D)\) and \(\text{mdeg}\zeta (D)\) are virtual link invariants. 

The main result of this paper is: let \(k(D)\) be the number of virtual crossings of a virtual diagram \(D\), then \(\text{deg}\zeta (D) \leq k(D)\) and \(\text{mdeg}\zeta (D) \geq -k(D)\). By the above result, we see that if \(\text{deg}\zeta (D) = k(D)\) then \(D\) has minimal possible number of virtual crossings. In section 3, the authors investigate virtual diagrams with this property, and construct infinite series of pairwise distinct minimal virtual knot diagrams. In the last section, some conjectures and problems are addressed.

title.title: On virtual crossing number estimates for virtual links

editorial_contributions.text: Two component classical links having zero linking number can be studied using virtual knot theory. Suppose that \(L=J \sqcup K\) is such a classical link with \(J\) fibered. The infinite cyclic cover of \(J\) is a thickened oriented surface \(\Sigma \times \mathbb{R}\). Since the linking number is \(0\), \(K\) lifts to a knot \(K'\) in \(\Sigma \times \mathbb{R}\). The virtual cover of \(K\) is the projection of \(K\) to an oriented virtual knot \(\upsilon\). Of course, there are infinitely many such lifts \(K'\) and potentially infinitely many different \(\upsilon\). There are many interesting situations however where \(\upsilon\) is an invariant of \(L\). For example, this occurs when \(K\) is ``close'' to a fiber of \(J\) (i.e. can be drawn as a diagram on a fiber \(\Sigma\) of \(J\)). \newline The authors of this paper apply the virtual cover construction to Kauffman and Manturov's generalization of the Kuperberg \(sl(3)\)-invariant to virtual knots. This is an invariant evaluated in \(\mathbb{Z}[A,A^{-1}][\mathscr{T}]\), where \(\mathscr{T}\) is the set of connected trivalent directed graphs containing neither bigons nor quadrilaterals, and each vertex is either a sink or a source. \newline The main application is to minimal diagrams of links \(L\) as above relative to a fixed fiber \(\Sigma\). If a particular state \(\upsilon_{us}\) in the generalized \(sl(3)\)-invariant is irreducible, then \(K'\) has the minimal number of double points in the projection to \(\Sigma\). The authors provide a non-trivial computation to illustrate their result.

title.title: Flat-virtual knot: introduction and some invariants

editorial_contributions.text: This book explains the authors' current work with \(G_n^k\) groups (\(k\)-free braid groups with \(n\) strands), focusing on picture-valued invariants -- those whose values are geometric constructions, like graphs or polyhedra. In [``Non-Reidemeister Knot Theory and Its Applications in Dynamical Systems, Geometry, and Topology'', Preprint, \url{arXiv:1501.05208}] the first named author introduced such groups, proceeding from the hypothesis that ``if in some science an object has intersections of multiplicity \(k\), then such an object can be studied by \(k\)-braids and their generalizations.'' In topology, he first demonstrated this principle in terms of parity for the case of virtual knots [\textit{V. O. Manturov}, Sb. Math. 201, No. 5, 693--733 (2010; Zbl 1210.57010)]. More generally, if any dynamical system describing a motion of \(n\) particles possesses a nice codimension 1 property governed by exactly \(k\) particles, then it possesses topological invariants valued in \(G_n^k\). Since these groups have many epimorphisms onto free products of cyclic groups, the authors note that invariants constructed from them are powerful and easy to compare, but that their methods fail ``when we try to deal with points on a 2-surface, since there may be infinitely many geodesics passing through two points.'' Thus they also explore ``another family of groups -- \(\Gamma_n^k\), which give rise to braids on arbitrary manifolds yielding invariants of arbitrary manifolds.'' The book concludes with a far ranging set of interesting problems.

editorial_contributions.text:
This monograph contains detailed accounts of two important ideas associated with virtual knots, extracted (in great part) from the broader discussion of virtual knot theory in a recent book by the first two authors [\textit{V. O. Manturov} and \textit{D. P. Ilyutko}, Virtual knots. The state of the art. Hackensack, NJ: World Scientific (2013; Zbl 1270.57003)].

The first of these important ideas is the notion of parity, which was introduced by \textit{V. O. Manturov} [Sb. Math. 201, No. 5, 693--733 (2010; Zbl 1210.57010)]. The origin of this notion lies in an observation of Gauss: if one walks along a classical knot diagram starting at a crossing, then one will encounter an even number of crossings before returning to the starting point. The definition of parity reflects the insight that although Gauss' observation does not hold for virtual knots (as virtual crossings are not counted), the crossings for which Gauss' observation fails are of a special type, which does not appear in classical knot theory.

The second of the important ideas is the notion of graph-links, different forms of which were introduced independently by \textit{D. P. Ilyutko} and \textit{V. O. Manturov} [J. Knot Theory Ramifications 18, No. 6, 791--823 (2009; Zbl 1189.57006)] and \textit{L. Zulli} and the reviewer [J. Knot Theory Ramifications 18, No. 12, 1681--1709 (2009; Zbl 1204.57009)]. The interlacement graph of an Euler circuit of a virtual link diagram \(D\) is the graph \(I(D)\) whose vertices are the crossings of \(D\), with two vertices \(v\) and \(w\) connected by an edge in \(I(D)\) if and only if when the Euler circuit is traversed beginning at \(v\), the crossing \(w\) is encountered precisely once before returning to \(v\). Many knot-theoretic ideas regarding virtual link diagrams yield graph-theoretic ideas about interlacement graphs in a natural way; for instance, Reidemeister moves on virtual link diagrams induce corresponding moves on interlacement graphs. The theory of graph-links is the result of extending these images of knot-theoretic ideas from interlacement graphs to general graphs. The monograph closes with two especially interesting extensions of this sort, which provide versions of the odd Khovanov homology for graph-links.

title.title: Parity in knot theory and graph-links

editorial_contributions.text:
In classical knot theory, the finite-type invariants (or Vassiliev invariants) are a family of knot invariants which extend to singular knots. With the help of Gauss diagrams, Polyak and Viro first gave a description of finite-type invariants with low orders, later Goussarov pointed out that each interger-valued finite-type invariant can be represented in this way.

Virtual knot theory which was introduced by L. Kauffman in the late 1990s can be regarded as a generalized knot theory. In virtual knot theory there are two notions of finite-type invariants, one was described by Goussarov, Polyak and Viro, the other one was introduced by L. Kauffman. Unlike the classical case, not every Kauffman finite-type invariant can be represented by the Polyak algebra.

In this paper, the authors construct an extension of the Polyak algebra with the help of parity. Here a parity means an axiomatic coloring of the arrows of a Gauss diagram with two elements. One is ODD, the other one is EVEN. The axioms make the colorings behave well under the Reidemeister moves. With this extended Polyak algebra, for Kauffman finite-type invariants the authors proves a result similar to the ones by Goussarov in classical knot theory. Finally a generating set for combinatorial \(P\)-formulae for Kauffman finite-type invariants of order two are listed, all of them are not of Goussarov-Polyak-Viro finite-type.

title.title: Group-valued invariant of knots in the full torus

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: We consider framed chord diagrams, i.e. chord diagrams with chords of two types. It is well known that chord diagrams modulo 4T-relations admit a Hopf algebra structure, where the multiplication is given by any connected sum with respect to the orientation. But in the case of framed chord diagrams a natural way to define a multiplication is not known yet. In this paper, we first define a new module \(\mathcal{M}_2\) which is generated by chord diagrams on two circles and factored by 4T-relations. Then we construct a ``parity'' map from the module of framed chord diagrams into \(\mathcal{M}_2\) and a weight system on \(\mathcal{M}_2\). Using the map and weight system we show that a connected sum for framed chord diagrams is not a well-defined operation. In the end of the paper we touch linear diagrams, the circle replaced by a directed line.

title.title: A parity map of framed chord diagrams

editorial_contributions.text:
In [Sb. Math. 201, No. 5, 693--733 (2010; Zbl 1210.57010)], \textit{V. O. Manturov} introduced the notion of parity into the study of different knot theories, especially virtual knots. A classical crossing in a knot diagram \(D\) is said to be even (odd) if on transversing the diagram \(D\) from the crossing until it returns, the number of classical crossings encountered is even (odd). Alternatively, in the Gauss diagram of \(D\), the arrow corresponding to the crossing passes an even (odd) number of other arrows. A \textit{parity} is a function on crossings valued in \(\{0, 1\}\) (where \(0\) and \(1\) stand for an even and odd crossing, respectively) and behaving nicely with respect to Reidemeister moves so that the parity allows one to refine many invariants, and construct new invariants in some knot theories. In some sense, odd crossings are responsible for non-triviality of knot diagrams, and one can prove many minimality and non-triviality theorems starting with some parity. A typical example of a parity is the \textit{Gaussian parity}, which is defined by assigning to each arrow \(x\) of the Gauss diagram \(D\) of a virtual knot \(K\) a \(0\) or a \(1\) according to whether the number of the arrows in \(D\) intersecting \(x\) is even or odd. Indeed, such an assignment behaves nicely under the Reidemeister moves. The parity theory now leads to a new perspective in virtual knot theory, the theory of cobordisms in two-dimensional surfaces, and other new domains of topology.

One goal of the paper under review is to generalize the notion of parity and to construct the parity with coefficients from an abelian group. Another goal is to classify parities for different knot theories (i.e., classical knots, virtual knots, free knots, flat knots, etc.). More precisely, the authors introduce the notion of parity with coefficients in an abelian group rather than \(\mathbb Z_2=\{0, 1\}\) and investigate the generalized parities for different knot theories. The authors describe how to construct parities from homology classes and indicate how to construct characteristic homology classes from a knot itself; these classes lead to concrete parities. The authors also deduce some basic properties of parity from the parity axioms and show that for some knot theories any parity can be obtained from one parity, called the universal parity. Especially, it is verified that there is only one non-trivial parity for free knots, the Gaussian parity. The authors also show that in the case of flat knots all parities originate from homology groups of underlying surfaces and, at the same time, allow one to localize the global homological information about the ambient space at crossings. The authors conclude the paper with some applications of parity. Firstly, they construct a functorial map from knots to knots which allows us to reformulate some theorems from Manturov [loc. cit.] for parities with coefficients from an abelian group and to extend some invariants. Secondly, for any parity valued in \(\{0, 1\}\) they give the parity bracket valued in the linear space \(\mathbb Z_2\mathfrak G\) that generalizes the Kauffman bracket polynomial and is an easily computed and highly distinguishable invariant for virtual knots, where \(\mathfrak G\) is the set of all equivalence classes of framed graphs with one unicursal component modulo second Reidemeister moves.

For the entire collection see [Zbl 1284.57003].

title.title: From chord parity to chord index

editorial_contributions.text:
The concept of parity and its application to knots is introduced in this text. Section 1 of the book is an introduction to virtual, flat and free knots. Parity is introduced in Section 2. Parity is a mapping from the set of crossings in the knot diagram to a group \( A\): \(p_K V(K) \rightarrow A\). Parity respects the properties based on the Reidemeister moves. For crossings \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) in a Reidemeister II move, \(p_K(v_1) + p_K(v_2) = 0\). For \(v_1,v_2,\) and \(v_3\) in a Reidemeister III move, \(p_K (v_1) + p_K (v_2) + p_K (v_3) = 0\). Several different methods of defining \(p_k\) are introduced, including a parity where \(A=H_1(S,\mathbb{Z}_2)/[K]\). The authors remark that ``when we deal with curves on a fixed surface, all possible parities for such curves are closely connected with (co)homology classes''. The chapter discusses how to construct parity from homology classes and how to construct characteristic homology classes from the knot.

Section 3 introduces the concept of universal parity. A parity \(p_u\) with coefficients in \(A_u\) is universal if for any parity \(p\) with coefficients in \(A\) there exists a unique homomorphism of groups \( \rho: A_u \rightarrow A\) such that \( \rho_K = \rho \circ (p_u)_K \) for any diagram \(K\). Key results in this section include the following. For free knots, Gaussian parity is the universal parity and the only possible parity. The sum of parities in the chords of a polygon (in a Gauss diagram) are zero. Any parity on virtual knots is trivial on a classical knot.

Section 4 introduces applications of parity. Knot invariants are constructed using parity. The authors begin by defining a functorial map from a knot to the category of virtual knot diagrams. The map is defined using parity. Using the image of the functorial map, the authors construct a variety of bracket invariants of the diagram. Applications of this process include odd irreducible Gauss diagrams. Section 5 concludes the volume, introducing cobordisms of free knots and obstructions to sliceness.

title.title: V. V. Trofimov's legacy in Lie theory

editorial_contributions.text:
Summary: In this paper we discuss the latest achievements in graph-link theory created by the first two authors in 2008-2009. This theory is a far-reaching generalization of classical and virtual knot theory and originates from the notion of the intersection graph (of a chord diagram). For a given graph a chord diagram having this graph as its intersection graph may not exist, however many invariants of classical and virtual knots can be extended to the theory of graph-links, in particular, Khovanov homology. Here we construct invariants of graph-links, many of them are based on the notion of parity due to the second author. We derive new properties of graph-links, which do not exist in the realizable case, and present non-realizable graph-links (i.e. such graph-links which have no representative realizable by a chord diagram), define an orientation for graph-links and construct the theory of Khovanov homology for graph-links.

title.title: Preface

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: This meeting concentrated on topological invariants in low dimensional topology and knot theory. We include both three and four dimensional manifolds in our phrase ``low dimensional topology''. The intent of the conference was to understand the reach of knot theoretic invariants into four dimensions, including results in Khovanov homology, variants of Floer homology and quandle cohomology and to understand relationships among categorification, topological quantum field theories and four dimensional manifold invariants as in particular Seiberg-Witten invariants.
